category_title: Pre-engaged students with organizational and focus challenges
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class literacy lesson at the beginning of the school year with the goal of seeing themselves as a reader.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, it is time for our whole-class literacy lesson. Please sit and listen to the instruction so we can practice seeing ourselves as readers.

STUDENT: I came to school to learn!

TUTOR: That is great. Now please focus on what I am saying.

STUDENT: (Wiggles around and points at a neighbor) Look at what he is doing.

TUTOR: Please keep your eyes up here and listen to the lesson.

STUDENT: (Picks up a found piece of string from the floor and starts twisting it around his fingers, completely fascinated by it instead of the teacher)

options.A: Sends a clear message to the student regarding the tutor's dissatisfaction with their distracted behavior during the literacy lesson.
options.B: Deletes some suggested activities that are overly repetitive and transforms what could be solitary tasks into supportive group efforts.
options.C: Gives the student stars and applause, using stickers and clapping as rewards for paying attention to the literacy instruction.
options.D: Gives the student a warning first, followed by a ten-minute timeout if they do not desist from playing with the string.
